key_insight: Two distinct nitrogen coordination sites in HATCN enable a Co-coordinated porous network on Ag(111) with three inequivalent molecular environments and site-specific electronic properties.
engineering_relevance: Selective metal coordination offers a route to tailor porous surface architectures and local electronic structure at the molecular level.
method: STM imaging of HATCN network restructuring upon Co coordination.
Momentum-resolved photoemission to probe electronic states.
Density functional theory to interpret coordination and charge transfer.
evidence_signal: STM reveals three structurally and electronically inequivalent molecules in a 6:3:1 ratio, while photoemission and DFT identify site-specific charge transfer from Co into the former HATCN LUMO.
watch_item: The findings concern Co–HATCN on Ag(111); transferability to other substrates or device conditions remains unestablished.
paper_title: Role of site-specific coordination for the structural and electronic properties of a Co-HATCN network on silver
